# Likely Causes of Mild Wrist Pain from Desk Work

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/hand-index-thumb.svg

A 34-year-old office worker with **3 weeks of mild wrist pain** after more keyboard use most commonly has an **overuse/strain problem** rather than an emergency. The pattern you described fits repetitive stress from typing, mouse use, or wrist posture.

# Practical Ergonomic Changes and Self-Care Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

## Common causes to consider
- **Tendon irritation / tendinopathy**: ache with repeated typing, clicking, or gripping.
- **Muscle strain from wrist extension**: wrists bent upward on the keyboard or desk edge pressure.
- **Early repetitive strain injury**: pain that builds through the workday and improves with rest.
- **Mild nerve irritation**: can happen even before numbness appears, especially with prolonged wrist pressure or awkward hand position.
- **Joint or soft-tissue irritation**: less likely here because there is no swelling, redness, fever, or injury.

## Ergonomic changes that usually help
- Keep **wrists neutral**: straight, not bent up, down, or to the side.
- Move the **keyboard closer** so you are not reaching forward.
- Keep **elbows near 90 degrees** and shoulders relaxed.
- Use a **light touch** on keys; avoid “bottoming out” hard.
- Let the **mouse sit close** to the keyboard; avoid repeated reaching.
- Consider a **vertical mouse** or different mouse size if clicking triggers pain.
- Raise or lower the **chair/desk** so forearms are roughly parallel to the floor.
- Avoid resting the wrist on a hard edge while typing; support the **forearm** instead.
- Take **microbreaks**: 30–60 seconds every 20–30 minutes, plus a longer break each hour.
- If using a laptop, add a **separate keyboard and mouse** and elevate the screen.

## Self-care steps you can start now
- **Reduce the trigger load** for 1–2 weeks: shorter typing bursts, more breaks, more voice dictation if possible.
- **Ice after work** for 10–15 minutes if it feels irritated; use a cloth barrier.
- **Gentle range-of-motion**: slowly open/close the hand, flex/extend the wrist within comfort.
- **Avoid painful strengthening** at first; do not push through sharp pain.
- If you normally can take them safely, **over-the-counter pain relief** may help short-term, but follow label directions and avoid if you have reasons not to use them.
- Watch for patterns: note whether pain is worse with **typing, mouse use, wrist extension, or gripping**.

## When to see a clinician
Seek medical evaluation if any of the following happen:
- Pain is **not improving after 2–4 weeks** of ergonomic changes and self-care
- Pain is **getting worse** or starts limiting daily tasks
- You develop **numbness, tingling, weakness, dropping objects, or hand clumsiness**
- There is **swelling, redness, warmth, fever, or a new lump**
- Pain follows a **fall, twist, or other injury**
- You have **night pain** that wakes you up or persistent pain at rest
- Pain spreads into the **forearm, thumb, or fingers** or becomes sharp with specific movements

## Best next steps for this situation
- Make the desk setup more neutral today.
- Use microbreaks and reduce continuous typing time.
- Track whether pain improves over the next 1–2 weeks.
- If it persists beyond a month total or interferes with work, book a clinician visit or a physical/occupational therapy assessment.

# Quick Workday Adjustments

- **Keyboard**: keep it flat or slightly negative tilt; avoid wrist extension.
- **Mouse**: keep close, use a light grip, consider a different shape.
- **Posture**: sit back, feet supported, elbows by your sides.
- **Breaks**: 20-20-20 style visual breaks plus short hand/wrist breaks.
- **Task changes**: alternate typing, mouse work, and non-hand tasks when possible.

# Sources

- NHS overview of repetitive strain injury: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/repetitive-strain-injury-rsi/
- Mayo Clinic on wrist pain causes and care: https://www.mayoclinic.org/symptoms/wrist-pain/basics/causes/sym-20050776
- MedlinePlus on wrist pain: https://medlineplus.gov/wristinjuriesanddisorders.html
